Question: Why is my transmission working in reverse but not drive?
Old_Answer: Years ago this happened to me. I had to drive about 5 miles in reverse to get to a repair shop. Here’s an article listing various reasons this can happen: Car Won’t Go Forward But Will Reverse - Automatic Transmission Exchange
Answer_with_writing_sample: When a transmission works in reverse but not in drive, it usually indicates a problem with the transmission system itself. There are several potential causes for this issue. One common reason is low transmission fluid levels. The fluid is essential for lubricating the transmission components and ensuring proper operation. If the fluid is low, it can lead to insufficient pressure, which may allow the transmission to engage reverse but not drive. Another possibility is a malfunctioning valve body. The valve body controls the flow of transmission fluid and directs it to the appropriate gears. If there’s a blockage or a failure in this component, it could prevent the transmission from shifting into drive while still allowing reverse to function. Additionally, there could be issues with the transmission control module (TCM) or the shift linkage. If the TCM is not sending the correct signals to the transmission, or if the linkage is misaligned or damaged, it may result in the inability to shift into drive. Lastly, internal transmission damage, such as worn clutches or bands, could also be a factor. These components are crucial for engaging the drive gears, and if they are compromised, the transmission may only operate in reverse. It’s advisable to have a professional mechanic diagnose the issue to determine the exact cause and recommend the necessary repairs. Ignoring the problem could lead to further damage and more costly repairs down the line.
